To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the two secreted proteins MIC-1 and platelet derived factor A (PDGFA) are elevated in prostate cancer and adjacent histologically normal tissues compared to disease-free tissue, and that this elevation is indicative of field cancerization.
the secreted factors MIC-1 and PDCF-A are elevated in both prostate tumor and adjacent tissues when compared with disease-free tissues, defining field cancerizaton.

prostate tumors are surrounded by field cancerization, defined by deregulated expression of MIC-1, and PDGF-A, which may promote tumor development in adjacent tissue and contribute to tumor multifocility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of prostate tumorigenesis and the development of novel biomarkers.
understanding the molecular basis of prostate field cancer and its implications for prostate cancer prevention.

identifying and characterizing the molecular alterations that are associated with prostate field cancerization, and the potential clinical utility of these alterations in prostate cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prostate field cancerization is a molecular phenomenon, and the two secreted proteins MIC-1 and PFDG-A are molecular indicators of this phenomenon.
the expression of MIC-1, PDGF-A and the other markers of field cancerization is elevated in tumor and adjacent tissue compared to disease free tissue.
MIC-1 is a marker for field cancerization in prostate cancer and that PDGF-A is a potential marker of field cancerization in this disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prostate cancer is a disease of the prostate gland, not the prostate tumor.
prostate field cancerization is a molecular phenomenon that can be measured by the expression of MIC-1, PDGF-A and other protein markers.
prostate field cancerization can be defined by the deregulated expression of MIC-1, PDGF-A, EGR-1, and FAS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
field cancerization is an important biological concept in prostate cancer that needs to be taken seriously in the clinic.
prostate field cancerization is a real phenomenon that should be considered by pathologists and oncologists when evaluating prostate tissues.
prostate field cancerization is a common and important event in prostate tumorigenesis.
